```{r setup}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
```

```{r config}
index_species <- "{{STOCK_KEY}}"
source(here::here("R", "0_setup.R"))
source(here::here("R", "compile_functions.R"))
source(here::here("R", "plot_helpers.R"))

stock <- cfg$STOCK_KEY
sp <- tolower(cfg$SPECIES_NAME)
area_label <- if (length(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS)) {
  paste("ICES subareas", paste(unlist(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS), collapse = " and "))
} else cfg$REGION
over_cm <- cfg$OVER_CM
fish_label <- paste0("Fishable (≥ ", over_cm, " cm)")
n_fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = " ")
pct <- function(x, acc = 1) scales::percent(x, accuracy = acc)
list_values <- function(x) if (length(x) < 2) x else paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])

dt <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "compiled-data.rds"))
lengths <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "length-data.rds"))
compile_metadata <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "compile-metadata.rds"))
dt$cruiseseries <- order_cruise_series(dt$cruiseseries, dt$year)
cs_cols <- cruise_series_colours(levels(dt$cruiseseries))
lengths <- lengths |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(dt, haul_id, year, cruiseseries, geartype), by = "haul_id")
lw <- compile_metadata$lw
pos <- dplyr::filter(dt, biomass > 0)

# Long format of the two biomass products for figures
products <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::transmute(dt, haul_id, year, month, depth, geartype, cruiseseries,
                   longitudestart, latitudestart, product = "Total",
                   biomass, density = rho_biomass),
  dplyr::transmute(dt, haul_id, year, month, depth, geartype, cruiseseries,
                   longitudestart, latitudestart, product = fish_label,
                   biomass = biomass_fishable, density = rho_biomass_fishable)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(product = factor(product, levels = c("Total", fish_label)))
prod_cols <- stats::setNames(c("#0072B2", "#D55E00"), levels(products$product))
```

# Purpose

This document describes the compiled IMR bottom-trawl data for the `r sp` (*`r cfg$SPECIES_LATIN`*) survey indices in `r area_label` (stock `r cfg$STOCK_CODE`). It explains and shows the two kinds of data that enter the spatiotemporal sdmTMB models [@Vihtakari2026]: the station-based catches, which give total biomass, and the length measurements, which divide each catch into fishable (≥ `r over_cm` cm) and smaller fish.

The input is the compiled dataset written by the survey-selection document ([`r stock`-2-survey-selection](`r stock`-2-survey-selection.html)), which documents the stock area, haul filter, surveys, gear and timing; those are not repeated here. The output is a judgement of whether the total-biomass and fishable-biomass responses are fit to be modelled, and where their coverage is thin.

# Data

## Data collation

The data flow is shown in @fig-data-flow. Station-level catches give the complete haul roster with true zeros (hauls of surveys that recorded the species when it was caught) and the total-biomass response. Individual length measurements are used only to divide each positive catch into the fishable and non-fishable parts; they do not change the total.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-data-flow
%%| fig-cap: "Data flow from the IMR Biotic database to the two model responses. Station catches give total biomass directly; individual lengths, converted to weight with the length–weight relationship, give the fishable share of each catch."
flowchart LR
  A["IMR Biotic database<br/>(BioticExplorerServer)"] --> B["Station catches<br/>stnall"]
  A --> C["Individual lengths<br/>indall"]
  B --> D["Haul filter and<br/>survey selection"]
  D --> E["Haul roster with<br/>true zeros"]
  E --> F["Total biomass<br/>per haul"]
  C --> G["Raised length<br/>distribution per haul"]
  G --> H["Weight-at-length<br/>(length–weight fit)"]
  H --> I["Fishable share<br/>of haul biomass"]
  F --> J["Total biomass density"]
  F --> K["Fishable biomass density"]
  I --> K
```

### Station-level data

The station-level dataset has one row per retained bottom-trawl haul. The `r sp` catch weight (`biomass`, kg) is summed over the catch samples of a haul, and hauls without `r sp` in an included survey are true zeros. Swept-area biomass density is

$$
\rho = \frac{B}{d \times w / 1852},
$$

where $B$ is the catch weight (kg), $d$ the towed distance (nmi) and $w$ the effective trawl width, `r if (length(cfg$GEAR_WIDTHS)) paste0(cfg$GEAR_WIDTH, " m by default and ", paste0(names(cfg$GEAR_WIDTHS), " ", unlist(cfg$GEAR_WIDTHS), " m", collapse = ", "), " (GEAR_WIDTHS; see the survey selection)") else paste0(cfg$GEAR_WIDTH, " m for every trawl")`, giving density in kg/nmi². The models use this density as the response (`EFFORT: density` in `config.yaml`); with a logit-link delta family this is equivalent to modelling the catch with the log swept area as an offset, whereas with a Poisson-link delta family it is not, because an offset there also enters the encounter probability.

### Individual-level data

The individual-level dataset contains the `r sp` length records from the retained hauls. Lengths are converted from metres to centimetres, and records outside `r compile_metadata$length_limits[1]`–`r compile_metadata$length_limits[2]` cm are removed as gross errors (`r compile_metadata$n_length_outliers` records). When a catch sample contains $m$ measured fish and a catch of $n$ fish, each measured fish represents $n/m$ fish (the raising factor); without a count the factor is one. `r cs <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "length-data.rds")) |> dplyr::summarise(n_ind = dplyr::n(), cc = dplyr::first(catchcount), .by = c("haul_id", "catchsampleid")); paste0("The catches of ", sp, " are small, and ", pct(mean(!is.na(cs$cc) & cs$n_ind >= cs$cc)), " of the catch samples were measured completely", if (any(is.na(cs$cc))) paste0(" (", pct(mean(is.na(cs$cc)), 0.1), " lack a count)") else "", ", so the raising factor is one for nearly all fish. The length samples of ", sp, " are not stratified by length in any cruise series, so the raised distribution represents the catch.")`

## Length-based data

Individual weight is predicted for every measured fish from the length–weight relationship $W = aL^b$ fitted to the survey fish with recorded weight (@fig-length-weight), so that measured and unmeasured weights are treated alike. For fish $i$ in a haul with raising factor $s_i$ and predicted weight $w_i$, the fishable share of the haul biomass is

$$
p = \frac{\sum_{i:\,L_i \ge `r over_cm`} s_i w_i}{\sum_i s_i w_i},
$$

and the fishable biomass is $B_f = pB$, with density $\rho_f = B_f / (d \times w / 1852)$. The fishable part therefore never exceeds the total, and the length data only redistribute the recorded catch. The threshold `r over_cm` cm is the length at which the Norwegian reference-fleet longline catches reach `r round(100 * (cfg$FISHABLE_PROP %||% 0.5))` % of their modal frequency; its derivation is documented in the *Fishable length* section of [`r stock`-0-background](../background/`r stock`-0-background.html#fishable-length).

Positive hauls without length measurements receive the biomass-weighted mean fishable share of the same survey, or, if no fish were measured in that survey, of the same cruise series and year, or of the cruise series. Zero hauls are zero for both products. Because the share is applied to the recorded catch weight, a survey that weighed the catch but did not measure the fish still contributes fishable biomass; it is not turned into a false zero, which would bias the fishable index downwards. The calculation is done by `add_fishable_biomass()` in `R/compile_functions.R` (@lst-compile-functions) when the survey-selection document compiles the data, and it is verified against hand-calculated cases and an independent recomputation in `ai/tests/test-fishable-biomass.R`.

# Analysis

## Dataset overview

The station-level dataset contains `r n_fmt(nrow(dt))` hauls from `r min(dt$year)`–`r max(dt$year)`, of which `r n_fmt(nrow(pos))` caught `r sp` and `r n_fmt(sum(dt$biomass_fishable > 0))` caught fishable `r sp`. The individual-level dataset contains `r n_fmt(nrow(lengths))` length records from `r n_fmt(dplyr::n_distinct(lengths$haul_id))` hauls (@tbl-overview). The cruise series differ in the share of positive hauls, in density and in the fishable share of the catch (@tbl-response-by-series).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-overview
tibble::tibble(
  Metric = c("Hauls", paste0("Hauls with ", sp), paste0("Hauls with fishable ", sp),
             "Zero fraction, total (%)", "Zero fraction, fishable (%)",
             "Length records", "Hauls with length records",
             "Length records with recorded weight",
             paste0("Positive hauls with fishable share from survey or series mean")),
  Value = c(n_fmt(nrow(dt)), n_fmt(nrow(pos)), n_fmt(sum(dt$biomass_fishable > 0)),
            sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(dt$biomass == 0)),
            sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(dt$biomass_fishable == 0)),
            n_fmt(nrow(lengths)), n_fmt(dplyr::n_distinct(lengths$haul_id)),
            n_fmt(sum(!is.na(lengths$weight_kg))),
            n_fmt(sum(pos$fishable_imputed %in% c("survey mean", "series-year mean", "series mean"))))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Overview of the station-level and individual-level ", sp, " data."))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-response-by-series
dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(`Cruise series` = cruiseseries) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Hauls = dplyr::n(),
    `Positive (%)` = round(100 * mean(biomass > 0), 1),
    `Fishable positive (%)` = round(100 * mean(biomass_fishable > 0), 1),
    `Median positive density (kg/nmi²)` = round(stats::median(rho_biomass[biomass > 0]), 1),
    `Total catch (kg)` = round(sum(biomass)),
    `Fishable share (%)` = round(100 * sum(biomass_fishable) / sum(biomass), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Station-level responses by cruise series. Density is swept-area biomass density in hauls with ", sp, "; fishable share is the fishable part of the total catch."))
```

### Response distribution

The response is zero-inflated and right-skewed (@fig-response-dist): most hauls are zeros, and the positive densities span several orders of magnitude. This shape is what delta (hurdle) model families describe with separate occurrence and positive-density components.

```{r}
#| label: fig-response-dist
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Distribution of swept-area biomass density of total and fishable ", sp, " in positive hauls (logarithmic x-axis). The share of zero hauls is given in each panel.")'
zero_lab <- products |>
  dplyr::group_by(product) |>
  dplyr::summarise(label = paste0("Zeros: ", sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(density == 0)), " %\nPositive: ",
                                  n_fmt(sum(density > 0))), .groups = "drop")
products |>
  dplyr::filter(density > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(density, fill = product)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, colour = NA) +
  geom_text(data = zero_lab, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.3, size = 2.8) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = prod_cols, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~product) +
  labs(x = "Density (kg/nmi²)", y = "Hauls")
```

## Station-level data

### Spatial distribution

Total and fishable biomass density are mapped for all years combined in @fig-density-map. The fishable fish occur in the same areas as the total catch, but in fewer hauls.

```{r density-map-base}
n_years <- dplyr::n_distinct(dt$year)
base_density <- ggOceanMaps::basemap(data = dt, legends = FALSE, base_size = 8,
                                     rotate = TRUE, expand.factor = 1,
                                     land.col = "grey85", land.border.col = "grey60")
density_map_height <- map_fig_height(base_density, ncol = 2, extra = 1, side = 0.4)
```

```{r, fig.height = density_map_height}
#| label: fig-density-map
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Biomass density of total (left) and fishable (right) ", sp, " in all retained hauls, all years combined. Grey crosses: zero catch; circles: positive hauls, size and colour by density (kg per nmi²).")'
base_density +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(
    data = dplyr::filter(products, density == 0),
    aes(longitudestart, latitudestart), shape = 3, size = 0.2, colour = "grey50",
    alpha = 0.4, crs = 4326) +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(
    data = dplyr::arrange(dplyr::filter(products, density > 0), density),
    aes(longitudestart, latitudestart, size = density, colour = density),
    alpha = 0.8, crs = 4326) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(trans = "log10", option = "plasma", direction = -1,
                         labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE),
                         name = "Density (kg/nmi²)") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 3, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~product) +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(), axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"))
```

### Annual distribution

The annual maps show the hauls of each year: where the surveys sampled, and how many positive hauls each year gives the models for total biomass (@fig-density-annual-total) and fishable biomass (@fig-density-annual-fishable). Years with few positive hauls, or with positive hauls only in part of the area, carry little information on the year-specific spatial pattern that the spatiotemporal fields estimate.

```{r density-annual-base}
annual_ncol <- 6
# Limits from the positive hauls, so that the panels are not dominated by empty survey area
base_annual <- ggOceanMaps::basemap(data = dplyr::filter(products, density > 0),
                                    legends = FALSE, base_size = 6, rotate = TRUE,
                                    expand.factor = 1.05, land.col = "grey95",
                                    land.border.col = "grey70")
annual_map_height <- map_fig_height(base_annual, ncol = annual_ncol,
                                    nrow = ceiling(n_years / annual_ncol), extra = 1.2,
                                    side = 0.2)
```

```{r, fig.height = annual_map_height}
#| label: fig-density-annual-total
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Annual distribution of the retained hauls with total biomass density of ", sp, ". Dark crosses: zero catch; circles: positive hauls, size and colour binned by quantiles of the positive densities (kg per nmi², bins common to all years). The map extent covers the positive hauls.")'
plot_annual_density(dplyr::filter(products, product == "Total"), base_annual,
                    ncol = annual_ncol)
```

```{r, fig.height = annual_map_height}
#| label: fig-density-annual-fishable
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Annual distribution of the retained hauls with fishable (≥ ", over_cm, " cm) biomass density of ", sp, ". Dark crosses: zero fishable catch; circles: hauls with fishable ", sp, ", size and colour binned by quantiles of the positive densities (kg per nmi², bins common to all years). The map extent covers the positive hauls.")'
plot_annual_density(dplyr::filter(products, product == fish_label), base_annual,
                    ncol = annual_ncol)
```

### Survey coverage by year

The cruise series sample different parts of the area, and the mix of series changes over the years (@fig-coverage-annual). `r cov <- dt |> dplyr::summarise(first = min(year), last = max(year), .by = "cruiseseries"); paste0("The series cover ", list_values(paste0(cov$cruiseseries, " (", cov$first, "–", cov$last, ")")), ".")` `r oth <- dt |> dplyr::summarise(share = mean(cruiseseries == "Other"), .by = "year"); early <- oth$share[oth$year < 2004]; if (length(early)) paste0("The irregular Other surveys hold up to ", pct(max(early)), " of the hauls of a year before 2004, and ", pct(mean(oth$share[oth$year >= 2004])), " on average from 2004.") else ""` A change in coverage can move the index if the model does not predict the unsampled cells well; the regional split, the leave-one-survey-out refits and the sensitivity analyses in the report test this.

```{r coverage-base}
base_cov <- ggOceanMaps::basemap(data = dt, legends = FALSE, base_size = 6, rotate = TRUE,
                                 expand.factor = 1.02, land.col = "grey95", land.border.col = "grey70")
cov_map_height <- map_fig_height(base_cov, ncol = annual_ncol, nrow = ceiling(n_years / annual_ncol),
                                 extra = 1, side = 0.2)
```

```{r, fig.height = cov_map_height}
#| label: fig-coverage-annual
#| fig-cap: "Retained hauls by year, coloured by cruise series."
base_cov +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(data = dt, aes(longitudestart, latitudestart, colour = cruiseseries),
                                size = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, crs = 4326) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cs_cols, name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +
  facet_wrap(~year, ncol = annual_ncol) +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(), axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 7, margin = margin(1, 0, 1, 0)),
        panel.spacing = unit(0.05, "lines"), legend.position = "bottom")
```

### Prediction grid

```{r prediction-region}
region_file <- here::here(cfg$PREDICTION_REGION_FILE %||%
                            file.path(cfg$SOURCE_DIR %||% "data/source", paste0(stock, "-prediction-region.gpkg")))
# Built and applied in the survey selection (<stock>-2-survey-selection.qmd)
region <- sf::read_sf(region_file) |> sf::st_transform(cfg$CRS)
# Depth-limited grid preview (the model fit builds the final grid the same way)
max_depth <- cfg$MAX_DEPTH %||% 1000
grid_base <- sdmTMBexperiments::make_prediction_grid(region, resolution = cfg$GRID_KM,
                                                     max_depth = max_depth, drop_isolated = TRUE)
if (!is.null(cfg$MIN_DEPTH)) grid_base <- grid_base[grid_base$depth >= cfg$MIN_DEPTH, ]
saveRDS(grid_base, file.path(out_dir, "prediction-grid-base.rds"))
grid_pts <- data.frame(x = grid_base$X * 1000, y = grid_base$Y * 1000) |>  # grid is in km
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = cfg$CRS) |>
  sf::st_transform(4326)
region_km2 <- as.numeric(sf::st_area(sf::st_union(region))) / 1e6
grid_km2 <- nrow(grid_base) * cfg$GRID_KM^2
n_pos_deep <- sum(pos$depth > max_depth, na.rm = TRUE)
base_region <- ggOceanMaps::basemap(data = dt, legends = FALSE, base_size = 8, rotate = TRUE,
                                    expand.factor = 1, land.col = "grey85",
                                    land.border.col = "grey60")
region_map_height <- map_fig_height(base_region, extra = 0.6)
```

The prediction region was built and applied in the survey selection ([`r stock`-2-survey-selection](`r stock`-2-survey-selection.html)), so all hauls in this report lie inside it (@fig-prediction-region). Within the region, the prediction grid keeps the `r cfg$GRID_KM`-km cells between land and `r max_depth` m depth (GEBCO, `ggOceanMaps::get_depth()`): `r n_fmt(nrow(grid_base))` cells, `r n_fmt(round(grid_km2, -2))` km² of the `r n_fmt(round(region_km2, -2))` km² region. `r if (n_pos_deep == 0) paste0("No haul with ", sp, " is deeper than this limit.") else paste0(n_pos_deep, if (n_pos_deep == 1) " haul" else " hauls", " with ", sp, if (n_pos_deep == 1) " is" else " are", " deeper than this limit; ", if (n_pos_deep == 1) "it stays" else "they stay", " in the model data but outside the prediction area.")` The model fit builds its grid in the same way.


```{r, fig.height = region_map_height}
#| label: fig-prediction-region
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Prediction grid for ", sp, ". Blue outline: the prediction region from the survey selection. Orange: hauls with ", sp, ". Blue squares: prediction-grid cells shallower than ", max_depth, " m. Grey crosses: hauls without ", sp, ".")'
(base_region +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = grid_pts, shape = 15, size = 0.25, colour = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.35,
                   inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = sf::st_transform(region, 4326), fill = NA,
                   colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(data = dplyr::filter(dt, biomass == 0),
    aes(longitudestart, latitudestart), shape = 3, size = 0.2, colour = "grey50", alpha = 0.4,
    crs = 4326) +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(data = pos, aes(longitudestart, latitudestart),
    colour = "#D55E00", size = 0.5, crs = 4326) +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank())) |>
  ggOceanMaps::reorder_layers()
```

### Through time

The annual mean density and the share of positive hauls show how the raw data change through the time series before any model standardisation (@fig-annual-response). These values mix changes in stock size with changes in survey coverage, gear and season, which the model accounts for only in part (through its covariates and random fields).

```{r}
#| label: fig-annual-response
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Annual raw data for total and fishable ", sp, ". A: share of hauls with ", sp, ". B: mean biomass density over all hauls (including zeros) with 95 % confidence intervals.")'
annual <- products |>
  dplyr::group_by(product, year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(positive = mean(density > 0), mean = mean(density),
                   se = stats::sd(density) / sqrt(dplyr::n()), .groups = "drop")
p_a <- ggplot(annual, aes(year, 100 * positive, colour = product)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = prod_cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Positive hauls (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
p_b <- ggplot(annual, aes(year, mean, colour = product)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = pmax(mean - 1.96 * se, 0), ymax = mean + 1.96 * se),
                  size = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = prod_cols) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Mean density (kg/nmi²)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
cowplot::plot_grid(p_a, p_b, ncol = 1, labels = "AUTO", align = "v", rel_heights = c(4, 5))
```

The share of empty hauls differs between the cruise series, which sample different areas and seasons, but changes little from year to year within the main series (@fig-zero-series). `r zs <- dt |> dplyr::summarise(z = mean(biomass == 0), n = dplyr::n(), .by = c("cruiseseries", "year")) |> dplyr::filter(n >= 20) |> dplyr::summarise(sd = stats::sd(z), med = stats::median(z), .by = "cruiseseries") |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(sd)); paste0("The median annual zero share is ", list_values(paste0(pct(zs$med), " (", zs$cruiseseries, ")")), ", with a between-year standard deviation of ", round(100 * min(zs$sd)), "–", round(100 * max(zs$sd)), " percentage points (series-years with at least 20 hauls).")` An abrupt change within a series would point to a change of protocol, gear or coverage.

```{r}
#| label: fig-zero-series
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Annual share of hauls without ", sp, " by cruise series, for series-years with at least 10 hauls; point size shows the number of hauls.")'
dt |>
  dplyr::summarise(zero = mean(biomass == 0), hauls = dplyr::n(), .by = c("cruiseseries", "year")) |>
  dplyr::filter(hauls >= 10) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, 100 * zero, colour = cruiseseries)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(size = hauls), alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cs_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 2.5, name = "Hauls") +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Hauls without catch (%)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

### Tow distance

Tow distance enters the response through the swept area. @fig-effort shows the retained tow distances by year and gear type. The density is divided by the swept area, so a change in the typical tow distance does not change its scale, but it changes the area each haul covers and so the chance that a haul catches the species. The distance is taken as correct; for `r n_fmt(sum(dt$speed_flag))` hauls whose distance and duration imply an implausible tow speed, the duration was set to missing in the survey selection.

```{r}
#| label: fig-effort
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "Tow distance of the retained hauls by year and gear type. Grey points: hauls (jittered); blue crossbars: annual mean with 95 % confidence interval."
eff <- dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(geartype, year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean = mean(distance), se = stats::sd(distance) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
                   n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(se = dplyr::coalesce(se, 0))
ggplot(dt, aes(year, distance)) +
  geom_jitter(colour = "grey60", size = 0.2, alpha = 0.4, width = 0.3, height = 0) +
  geom_crossbar(data = eff, aes(year, mean, ymin = mean - 1.96 * se, ymax = mean + 1.96 * se),
                colour = "#0072B2", width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~geartype) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2030, 5)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Tow distance (nmi)")
```

### Depth

Depth enters the models as a smooth term. The hauls with `r sp` cover a narrower depth range than the sampling effort (@fig-depth A), and both the density in positive hauls and the mean density including zeros vary with depth (@fig-depth B). The depth range of the data limits the depth range of the prediction grid.

```{r}
#| label: fig-depth
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Depth distribution of the data. A: bottom depth of all hauls and of hauls with ", sp, " (densities scaled to the same maximum; the deepest 0.5 % of hauls are outside the plotted range). B: biomass density against depth in hauls with ", sp, " (points; pseudo-logarithmic y-axis) and mean density of all hauls including zeros in 50-m depth bins with at least 20 hauls (lines). Zero hauls are not drawn as points.")'
depth_lim <- c(0, stats::quantile(dt$depth, 0.995, na.rm = TRUE))
depth_hauls <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(dt, group = "All hauls"),
  dplyr::mutate(pos, group = paste("Hauls with", sp))
)
p_a <- ggplot(depth_hauls, aes(depth, after_stat(scaled), fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5, colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey50", "#E69F00")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = depth_lim) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Scaled density", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
depth_means <- products |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(depth)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(depth_bin = floor(depth / 50) * 50 + 25) |>
  dplyr::group_by(product, depth_bin) |>
  dplyr::summarise(density = mean(density), n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::filter(n >= 20)
p_b <- products |>
  dplyr::filter(density > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(depth, density, colour = product)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = depth_means, aes(depth_bin), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = depth_means, aes(depth_bin), size = 1.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 1, base = 10),
                     breaks = c(0, 1, 10, 100, 1000, 1e4),
                     labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = depth_lim) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = prod_cols) +
  labs(x = "Bottom depth (m)", y = "Density (kg/nmi²)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
cowplot::plot_grid(p_a, p_b, ncol = 1, labels = "AUTO", align = "v", rel_heights = c(4, 5))
```

### Season and gear

Month and gear type are both confounded with cruise series, because each series samples in a fixed season, mostly with one gear (see the survey-selection document). `r switch(month_term(cfg), smooth = "Month enters the models as a smooth term", factor = "Month enters the models as a factor", none = "The models have no month term")`, and gear type `r if ("geartype" %in% unlist(cfg$FINAL_MODEL$TERMS)) "is a fixed effect" else "was dropped in the model selection"`. @fig-month-gear shows the raw positive densities by month and by gear type within cruise series; differences between gears within the same cruise series are the information a gear effect would be estimated from.

```{r}
#| label: fig-month-gear
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Biomass density of total ", sp, " in positive hauls by month (A) and by gear type within cruise series (B), logarithmic scale. Numbers under the month labels and below the boxes are positive hauls.")'
month_n <- dplyr::count(pos, month)
month_lab <- stats::setNames(paste0(1:12, "\n(", month_n$n[match(1:12, month_n$month)], ")"), 1:12)
month_lab <- sub("\\(NA\\)", "(0)", month_lab)
p_a <- ggplot(pos, aes(factor(month, levels = 1:12), rho_biomass)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.4, outlier.size = 0.4, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE, labels = month_lab) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  labs(x = "Month (positive hauls)", y = "Density (kg/nmi²)")
gear_n <- dplyr::count(pos, cruiseseries, geartype)
y_low <- min(pos$rho_biomass) / 3
p_b <- ggplot(pos, aes(cruiseseries, rho_biomass, fill = geartype)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4, linewidth = 0.3,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.75, preserve = "single")) +
  geom_text(data = gear_n, aes(cruiseseries, y_low, label = n, group = geartype),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.75, preserve = "single"), size = 2.5,
            inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gear_colours()) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density (kg/nmi²)", fill = "Gear type") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
cowplot::plot_grid(p_a, p_b, ncol = 1, labels = "AUTO", align = "v")
```

### Index year and design balance

The model's time step is the **index year** (`INDEX_YEAR_START_MONTH` = `r cfg$INDEX_YEAR_START_MONTH %||% 1`, labelled by the calendar year it `r cfg$INDEX_YEAR_LABEL %||% "start"`s). When surveys from several seasons are combined, every survey of one season must fall in the intended index year; @tbl-index-year shows how calendar months map to index years for each cruise series.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-index-year
if (!"index_year" %in% names(dt)) {   # data compiled before index years were added
  dt$index_year <- index_year(dt$year, dt$month, cfg$INDEX_YEAR_START_MONTH %||% 1L,
                              cfg$INDEX_YEAR_LABEL %||% "start")
}
knitr::kable(
  dt |>
    dplyr::group_by(cruiseseries) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      months = paste(sort(unique(month)), collapse = ", "),
      calendar_years = paste0(min(year), "–", max(year)),
      index_years = paste0(min(index_year), "–", max(index_year)),
      shifted_hauls = sum(index_year != year),
      .groups = "drop"
    ),
  caption = "Survey months, calendar years and index years by cruise series. Shifted hauls are assigned to an index year other than their calendar year."
)
```

A cruise series or gear whose share of the hauls swings between years is confounded with the year effect: its catchability difference is then estimated from few years and can be read as a trend. @tbl-design-balance flags factor levels whose annual share ranges over more than 0.5, and @fig-design-balance shows the gear shares.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-design-balance
balance <- lapply(intersect(c("cruiseseries", "geartype"), names(dt)), function(v) {
  b <- design_balance(dt, v, time_col = "index_year")
  dplyr::mutate(b$shift, factor = v, level = as.character(.data[[v]]), .before = 1) |>
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::all_of(v))
})
knitr::kable(
  dplyr::bind_rows(balance),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Annual haul share by cruise series and gear type: years present, minimum and maximum share, and whether the share range exceeds 0.5."
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-design-balance
#| fig-cap: "Share of retained hauls by gear type in each index year."
design_balance(dt, "geartype", time_col = "index_year")$counts |>
  ggplot(aes(index_year, share, fill = geartype)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gear_colours()) +
  labs(x = "Index year", y = "Share of hauls", fill = "Gear type")
```

<!-- Describe the supported finding. A flagged level needs a decision before modelling: drop it, model it, or justify the confounding. -->

### Terminal-year completeness

Some data typically arrive after the assessment (for example one nation's or one vessel's hauls). Set `LATE_COMPONENTS` in `config.yaml` to the compiled-data column and values concerned; @tbl-late-components then shows their haul counts in recent index years, so an incomplete terminal year is visible. The robustness section of the final report refits the index without them in the terminal year.

```{r, eval=!is.null(cfg$LATE_COMPONENTS)}
#| label: tbl-late-components
late_col <- cfg$LATE_COMPONENTS$column
recent <- dplyr::filter(dt, index_year > max(index_year) - 5)
knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame.matrix(table(recent$index_year,
                             ifelse(recent[[late_col]] %in% cfg$LATE_COMPONENTS$values,
                                    "late component", "other"))),
  caption = "Retained hauls in the last five index years from the components that usually arrive late."
)
```

## Length-based data

### Length–weight relationship

The length–weight relationship was fitted on the log scale to `r n_fmt(lw$n)` survey fish with recorded weight, after removing `r compile_metadata$n_lw_outliers` outliers with an absolute standardised residual above `r compile_metadata$lw_outlier_sd`, using `ggFishPlots::plot_lw(outlier.sd = `r compile_metadata$lw_outlier_sd`)`. The fit gave $W = `r signif(lw$a, 3)` L^{`r round(lw$b, 3)`}$ with $W$ in kg and $L$ in cm (@fig-length-weight).

```{r}
#| label: fig-length-weight
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Length and weight of ", sp, " with recorded weight in the retained hauls (ggFishPlots::plot_lw). The line is the fitted length–weight relationship used to predict weight at length; crosses are the outliers removed from the fit.")'
compile_metadata$lw_plot
```

```{r lw-sex}
# Length-weight by sex (Biotic sex codes: 1 female, 2 male)
lw_sex <- lengths |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(weight_kg), weight_kg > 0, as.character(sex) %in% c("1", "2")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sex = factor(as.character(sex), levels = c("1", "2"), labels = c("female", "male")))
lw_m0 <- stats::lm(log(weight_kg) ~ log(length_cm), lw_sex)
lw_m1 <- stats::lm(log(weight_kg) ~ log(length_cm) * sex, lw_sex)
lw_len <- c(40, 60, 80, 100)
lw_ratio <- exp(stats::predict(lw_m1, data.frame(length_cm = lw_len, sex = "female")) -
                stats::predict(lw_m1, data.frame(length_cm = lw_len, sex = "male")))
```

The length–weight relationship is common to both sexes. Of the fish with recorded weight, `r n_fmt(nrow(lw_sex))` have a recorded sex; separate relationships by sex change the AIC by `r sprintf("%.1f", round(stats::AIC(lw_m1) - stats::AIC(lw_m0), 1) + 0)`, and the predicted weight of a female is `r sprintf("%.2f", min(lw_ratio))`–`r sprintf("%.2f", max(lw_ratio))` times that of a male of the same length at `r min(lw_len)`–`r max(lw_len)` cm. The fishable share is a ratio of weights within a haul, so differences of this size do not change it noticeably. Maturity was not considered: it is recorded for a minority of the measured fish.

### Length distributions

The raised length distributions show which part of the population each cruise series catches relative to the fishable threshold (@fig-length-dist). The share of the catch above the threshold differs between cruise series, which is one reason why the fishable and total indices can diverge.

```{r}
#| label: fig-length-dist
#| fig-height: !expr 'ceiling(dplyr::n_distinct(lengths$cruiseseries) / 3) * 1.8 + 0.6'
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Raised length distributions of ", sp, " by cruise series (5-cm bins; each measured fish weighted by its raising factor). Dashed line: fishable threshold (", over_cm, " cm). n: measured fish.")'
len_n <- dplyr::count(lengths, cruiseseries, name = "n") |>
  dplyr::mutate(label = paste0("n = ", vapply(n, n_fmt, character(1))))
ggplot(lengths, aes(length_cm, weight = raising, fill = cruiseseries)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0, colour = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = over_cm, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(data = len_n, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 2.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs_cols, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~cruiseseries, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Raised number of fish")
```

The length composition also changes through time (@fig-length-year). Because the cruise-series mix changes between years, part of this change reflects survey coverage rather than the stock.

```{r}
#| label: fig-length-year
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Annual raised length composition of ", sp, ", all cruise series combined. Line: median length; ribbon: 10th–90th percentile. Dashed line: fishable threshold. Years with fewer than 10 measured fish are not shown.")'
wq <- function(x, w, p) {
  o <- order(x); x <- x[o]; w <- w[o]
  cw <- cumsum(w) / sum(w)
  x[which(cw >= p)[1]]
}
lengths |>
  dplyr::group_by(year) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() >= 10) |>
  dplyr::summarise(q10 = wq(length_cm, raising, 0.1), q50 = wq(length_cm, raising, 0.5),
                   q90 = wq(length_cm, raising, 0.9), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(year, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q10, ymax = q90), fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  geom_point(colour = "#0072B2", size = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = over_cm, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Length (cm)")
```

### Sample sizes

The number of hauls with `r sp` and of measured fish differs between cruise series and years (@fig-sample-size). `r m <- dplyr::count(lengths, haul_id, name = "measured"); pm <- dplyr::left_join(pos, m, by = "haul_id") |> dplyr::mutate(measured = dplyr::coalesce(measured, 0L)); paste0("A haul with ", sp, " has a median of ", stats::median(pm$measured), " measured fish, and ", pct(mean(pm$measured <= 5)), " of them have five or fewer.")` Series-years with few hauls carry little information on their own; their influence on the index is examined in the report (influence of cruises and hauls, leave-one-survey-out refits and the major-series sensitivity).

```{r}
#| label: fig-sample-size
#| fig-height: !expr '0.35 * dplyr::n_distinct(dt$cruiseseries) * 2 + 1.6'
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Hauls with ", sp, " (A) and measured ", sp, " (B) by cruise series and year. Numbers in the cells; blank: none.")'
ss <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::summarise(pos, n = dplyr::n(), .by = c("cruiseseries", "year")) |> dplyr::mutate(what = "A"),
  dplyr::summarise(lengths, n = dplyr::n(), .by = c("cruiseseries", "year")) |> dplyr::mutate(what = "B"))
lab_what <- c(A = paste("A) Hauls with", sp), B = paste("B) Measured", sp))
ggplot(ss, aes(year, cruiseseries, fill = log10(n))) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), size = 1.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, begin = 0.2, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~what, ncol = 1, labeller = labeller(what = lab_what)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = NULL)
```

### Fishable share and length coverage

`r n_fmt(sum(pos$fishable_imputed == "measured"))` of the `r n_fmt(nrow(pos))` positive hauls had measured lengths; the fishable share of the others was taken from the survey or cruise-series mean (@fig-length-coverage A). The annual fishable share of the total catch is shown in @fig-length-coverage B.

```{r}
#| label: fig-length-coverage
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("A: positive ", sp, " hauls by the source of their fishable share, by cruise series. B: fishable share of the total ", sp, " catch by year (all hauls combined); point size shows the number of positive hauls.")'
src_cols <- c(measured = "#0072B2", `survey mean` = "#56B4E9",
              `series-year mean` = "#E69F00", `series mean` = "#D55E00", none = "grey50")
p_a <- pos |>
  dplyr::count(cruiseseries, fishable_imputed) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fishable_imputed = factor(fishable_imputed, levels = names(src_cols))) |>
  ggplot(aes(cruiseseries, n, fill = fishable_imputed)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = src_cols, drop = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Positive hauls", fill = "Fishable share from") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
p_b <- dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(share = sum(biomass_fishable) / sum(biomass), n = sum(biomass > 0),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::filter(n > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, 100 * share)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), colour = "#D55E00") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 3, name = "Positive hauls") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Fishable share of catch (%)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
cowplot::plot_grid(p_a, p_b, ncol = 1, labels = "AUTO", align = "v", axis = "lr")
```

### Data checks

The automated checks in @tbl-data-checks look for errors that the haul filter cannot catch: unit or subsampling errors in catch weight and count, partly measured catches, inconsistent derived values, implausible tow speeds, ICES subareas in the area code that do not match the position (division boundaries differ between Biotic and the ICES polygons, so divisions are not compared), recorded depths that do not match the GEBCO depth, positive hauls outside the prediction region or deeper than the prediction grid, gaps in the time series, and hauls at the same date and position. Hauls at the same date and position are split by vessel and start time: hauls by different vessels are paired or comparison hauls, and hauls by one vessel at different times are repeated tows, often experiments with different tow durations or gear; neither is a duplicate. Only hauls by one vessel starting within 30 minutes of each other are possible double entries. No haul is removed on the basis of these checks; the flagged hauls are listed in `ai/review/` for inspection of the records.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data-checks
checks <- data_checks(dt, lengths, lw, region, ices_file = read_ices_areas(cfg),
                      max_depth = max_depth)
readr::write_csv(
  attr(checks, "same_position") |>
    dplyr::select(key, pair_type, haul_id, platformname, cruiseseries, gear, start_time,
                  distance, duration_min, biomass, count, depth),
  here::here("ai", "review", paste0(stock, "-same-position-hauls.csv"))
)
readr::write_csv(
  attr(checks, "flagged") |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(dt, haul_id, year, cruiseseries, gearname, biomass, count,
                                   distance, duration_min), by = "haul_id"),
  here::here("ai", "review", paste0(stock, "-flagged-hauls.csv"))
)
checks |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Flagged (%)` = round(100 * Flagged / Of, 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Automated data checks for the compiled ", sp, " data. Of: number of hauls or years checked."))
```

# Results and recommendations

**Ready for modelling.** The total-biomass response is complete for all `r n_fmt(nrow(dt))` hauls, of which `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(dt$biomass == 0))` % are true zeros. The fishable-biomass response is defined for every haul as well; `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(dt$biomass_fishable == 0))` % of the hauls have no fishable `r sp`.

**Usable with a stated limitation.** For `r n_fmt(sum(pos$fishable_imputed != "measured"))` positive hauls the fishable share is a survey or cruise-series mean rather than a measurement (@fig-length-coverage). The fishable share also depends on the predicted weight at length, so the fishable biomass is a modelled division of an observed catch.

**Examined in the model fits.** Depth, month and gear type all relate to density in the raw data (@fig-depth, @fig-month-gear), but these relations are confounded with cruise series and area. The model selection tests the gear and month terms and a cruise-series factor. How the changing survey mix affects the indices is examined in the report (leave-one-survey-out and single-survey indices).
